findings.title: Default update-strategy tests never enable rolling-updates
findings.body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when the update strategy is null, and the new code that sets spec.features.enabled to rolling-updates runs only for a non-null strategy. The parameterized image-change and cache-max-count tests call this helper with both null (the default strategy) and Recreate. The operator guide in this PR says that while the feature is preview it must be enabled or the operator fails, including for the default strategy that still decides rolling vs recreate on image changes. The default-strategy cases therefore never put rolling-updates on the Keycloak CR, which is the configuration users are told to set. Those tests either fail when the compatibility command rejects a feature-disabled server, or they pass only because operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image now bakes the feature into the test image and never cover the documented CR path. Enable the feature for every deployment this helper builds, before the null return. setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)) also replaces any features already on the CR instead of appending rolling-updates, so a deployment that already enables features loses them in the Recreate cases.

findings.title: Exit code 4 changed meaning from recreate to feature-disabled
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4 and is now 3, and 4 is reused as FEATURE_DISABLED. The update-compatibility check exit code is the public contract the guide tells automation to branch on. After this change an incompatible deployment exits 3 instead of 4, and exit 4 means the preview feature is off and no compatibility decision was made. Callers that observed the previous implementation (exit 4 = shut the deployment down and recreate) will treat a disabled feature as recreate-required, and will not treat a real incompatibility (now exit 3) as recreate-required, which can allow a rolling update the tool rejected or cause a full shutdown when the user only needed to enable the feature. The guide already listed 3 for recreate before this PR, so the old constant disagreed with the guide; if that text is the shipped contract, aligning the constant is right, but nothing in this PR updates operator production code that may still compare the job status to a literal 4. UpdateCommandDistTest does not assert either code, so CI will not catch a regression to the old value.

findings.title: New and renumbered compatibility exit codes are not asserted
findings.body: The distribution tests never check the exit codes this PR defines. testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts that stderr contains the disabled-feature message, and it only launches the metadata subcommand; it does not assert exit code 4, and there is no equivalent case for check. testWrongVersions only asserts the incompatibility error text after RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moved from 4 to 3, so a build that still exits 4 (now the feature-disabled code) would still pass. The guide tells automation to branch on these codes (0 rolling, 3 recreate, 4 feature disabled). Assert the process exit code for both subcommands when rolling-updates is off, and assert exit code 3 when the stored versions are incompatible.

findings.title: Documented --features flag replaces other enabled features
findings.body: The updatecompatibility doc macro now renders every example as bin/kc.sh update-compatibility <args> --features=rolling-updates. Keycloak gives CLI arguments precedence over KC_FEATURES and keycloak.conf, and features is a single list-valued option, not a set merged across sources. Copying the documented command therefore replaces any other explicitly enabled features with only rolling-updates. The same guide says every option from the real deployment must be present and that omitting options produces an incorrect rolling-versus-recreate outcome. The examples should tell users to add rolling-updates to their existing enabled-feature list rather than hard-coding a replacement --features value.
